# A local cross-body density theorem for regular support-face foliations

This is a concrete extension beyond facets and cone generators. It derives
compatibility of the ACTUAL three conditional surface densities from a
common normal foliation and tight midpoint support. It does not infer that
compatibility merely from log-concavity of each individual density.

The theorem is local and conditional on the explicit regular foliation
hypotheses below. No claim is made that arbitrary convex bodies admit a
countable covering by patches satisfying those hypotheses.

## 1. Regular patch and notation

Let K_-,K_0,K_+ be convex bodies in R^d with

    (K_-+K_+)/2 subset K_0.

Let U be an open subset of R^k and n:U->S^(d-1) a C^2 injective
immersion of rank k. Put m=d-1-k. Assume the three support heights

    h_i(t)=h_(K_i)(n(t))

are C^2 on U and satisfy

    h_0(t)=[h_-(t)+h_+(t)]/2       for every t in U.                (1)

Assume the support faces on this patch have affine dimension m and that
their relative interiors form regular boundary patches with their unique
outward normal equal to n(t). The precise use of this condition is that
the face parametrizations defined below are one-to-one on the chosen
patches and that their ordinary surface measure is given by their
(d-1)-dimensional area Jacobian. Local restrictions or omission of
surface-null exceptional sets are allowed, but the hypothesis is not
asserted for general Borel face partitions.

At each t let N(t) be an orthonormal k-frame for the column space of
Dn(t), and let E(t) be an orthonormal m-frame for

    L(t)=ker(n(t)^T) intersect ker(Dn(t)^T).

These frames may be chosen C^1 locally; all conclusions are local and
independent of the chosen orientation. Set

    R(t)=N(t)^T Dn(t).

It is invertible, with |det R|=sqrt(det(Dn^T Dn)). The k=0 case is treated
separately below.

## 2. Common affine coordinates for the actual faces

For any X in the support face K_i(n(t)), the function

    t' -> h_i(t')-n(t') dot X

is nonnegative and vanishes at t. Its first derivative therefore gives

    n(t) dot X=h_i(t),
    Dn(t)^T X=grad h_i(t).                        (2)

The solution space of these equations is a translate of L(t), which has
dimension m. Since the actual face has dimension m, this solution space
is its affine hull. Let a_i(t) be the unique solution perpendicular to
L(t). It depends C^1 on t because the common coefficient matrix has
constant full row rank. The actual face points have coordinates

    X_i(t,s)=a_i(t)+E(t)s,       s in F_i(t) subset R^m.             (3)

The coordinate face F_i(t) is compact and convex. The choice of a_i is
linear in (h_i,grad h_i), so (1) implies

    a_0=(a_-+a_+)/2.

For all s_- in F_-(t), s_+ in F_+(t), actual midpoint inclusion and tight
support consequently give

    (s_-+s_+)/2 in F_0(t),
    [X_-(t,s_-)+X_+(t,s_+)]/2
       =X_0(t,(s_-+s_+)/2).                       (4)

These are statements about the actual boundary faces, not an abstract
convex family replacing them.

## 3. The actual surface conditional density

Define the k by k matrix

    Q_i(t,s)=D^2h_i(t)-sum_(a=1)^d X_(i,a)(t,s) D^2 n_a(t).        (5)

It is symmetric positive semidefinite at every actual face point. Indeed
it is the Hessian, at a local minimum, of the nonnegative function in
Section 2 with X fixed. It is affine in the face coordinate s.

Differentiate (2) along a parametrized face point. The result is

    n^T D_t X_i=0,
    Dn^T D_t X_i=Q_i.                            (6)

Also D_s X_i=E. The columns of D_t X_i are tangent to the boundary and
can be written in the orthonormal frame [N,E] as [A_i;B_i], where
A_i=N^T D_t X_i. From Dn=N R and (6),

    R^T A_i=Q_i.

The coordinate matrix of [D_t X_i,D_s X_i] in that orthonormal tangent
frame is the block matrix

    [ A_i  0 ]
    [ B_i  I ].

Therefore its (d-1)-dimensional area Jacobian is exactly

    J_i(t,s)=|det A_i(t,s)|
            =det Q_i(t,s)/|det R(t)|.             (7)

In particular, on the regular patch the actual surface measure is

    d eta_i=J_i(t,s) dt ds.                       (8)

This uses a COMMON transverse reference dt for all three bodies. If one
instead normalizes each body's conditional law to be a probability, the
different normal-marginal factors must also be retained. Dropping those
factors would destroy the comparison below.

## 4. Cross-body determinant compatibility

Let s_0=(s_-+s_+)/2. Equations (1), (4), and (5) give the exact identity

    Q_0(t,s_0)=[Q_-(t,s_-)+Q_+(t,s_+)]/2.         (9)

For k>=1, the determinant inequality for positive semidefinite k by k
matrices gives

    J_0(t,s_0)^(1/k)
       >=[J_-(t,s_-)^(1/k)+J_+(t,s_+)^(1/k)]/2.  (10)

The common denominator |det R| in (7) is essential here. For completeness,
the matrix inequality can be proved directly. When A is positive definite,
conjugate B by A^(-1/2), with eigenvalues lambda_j>=0. The desired
inequality reduces to

    product_j(1+lambda_j) >=
                   [1+(product_j lambda_j)^(1/k)]^k.

For positive lambda_j this is Jensen's inequality for the convex function
x->log(1+exp x), applied to log lambda_j. Zero eigenvalues follow by
continuity, as do singular A by replacing A,B with A+epsilon I,B+epsilon I.

If m>=1, the elementary order of power means now gives

    J_0(t,s_0)
      >=[(J_-^(1/k)+J_+^(1/k))/2]^k
      >=[(J_-^(-1/m)+J_+^(-1/m))/2]^(-m).         (11)

The last expression is zero when either input density is zero. One may
also see the last inequality by putting the geometric mean between the
positive and negative power means. Thus (11) is exactly the capacity
inequality needed by variable-density midpoint selection in face
dimension m.

This derives a relation among DIFFERENT bodies. Individual concavity of
J_i^(1/k) on its own face follows as well from the affine matrix formula,
but that individual fact would not alone prove (11).

## 5. Actual conditional midpoint repair on this patch

Suppose the original same-normal endpoint crossflow has, relative to dt,
conditional endpoint measures gamma_(minus,t),gamma_(plus,t), of equal
mass, with

    gamma_(i,t)<=J_i(t,s) ds.

Let its old conditional endpoint pairing have midpoint law rho_old,t.
All these measures refer to the common normal n(t). For a fixed t with
m>=1, apply variable-density selection in R^m. Equation (11) bounds its
supremal midpoint capacity by J_0(t,s), and (4) puts every selected
midpoint in the actual middle face. Hence there exists a replacement
pair coupling with the same conditional endpoint marginals and

    rho_old,t<=_cx rho_t,
    rho_t<=J_0(t,s) ds.                           (12)

The comparisons are for full physical convex tests restricted to this
affine face. These statements use the unnormalized conditional measures
relative to dt, so the target in (12) is precisely the conditional middle
surface measure from (8).

Once a measurable family of these compact coupling choices is supplied,
the martingale rebuilding used in the polytopal theorem applies to the
whole patch: compose old midpoint to selected midpoint martingales, split
selected pairs into endpoints, retain old endpoint-source rows, and keep
the source, target, physical endpoint crossflows, and cap allocations.
The present note proves the geometric conditional-capacity input to that
assembly. It does not silently infer measurable selection from pointwise
existence.

## 6. The two boundary ranks

If k=0, the normal is fixed and m=d-1. The patch is an actual facet,
there is no transverse variable, and its density in Euclidean tangent
coordinates is one. The midpoint inclusion gives the capacity inequality
1>=H_m(1,1) with equality. This is exactly the already audited facet
repair; no 1/k expression is used.

If m=0 and k=d-1>=1, each support face is a singleton X_i(t). Its
conditional measure relative to dt is J_i(t) delta_(X_i(t)). A common
endpoint crossflow has mass a(t)<=min(J_-(t),J_+(t)). Equations (9)-(10)
give

    J_0(t)>=min(J_-(t),J_+(t))>=a(t).

Its unique midpoint is X_0(t), by (4). The old law is already dominated
by the actual middle conditional measure; no positive-dimensional
selection theorem is needed. This covers the point-output Jacobian case.

For d=1, k=m=0 describes an endpoint with counting surface measure one.
That case is likewise direct counting, as in the polytopal theorem.

## 7. Cone calibration and the unresolved general-body step

For the three-dimensional cone

    {(x,y,z):0<=z<=1, sqrt(x^2+y^2)<=z},

the lateral normal manifold is one-dimensional and the faces are
one-dimensional generators. With the usual angular coordinate and radial
parameter r, the surface element is sqrt(2) r dr dtheta. After normalizing
the normal marginal, the conditional probability density is 2r dr.
This nonconstant density is a special case of the affine determinant in
(7) with k=1. Compatible tight conical/developable patches of different
bodies satisfy the cross-body identity (9), so their repair follows from
(11), not just from the shape of the single cone density.

For arbitrary convex bodies, normal/face strata need not be presented by
the regular common foliation assumed here. The background disintegration
theorem of Caravenna and Daneri proves absolute continuity of face
conditional measures, but that conclusion alone does not establish the
cross-body determinant identity or inequality above. See their paper,
[The Disintegration of the Lebesgue Measure on the Faces of a Convex
Function](https://cvgmt.sns.it/media/doc/paper/1434/disFacceConvCD.pdf).

Extending (11) to those general conditional measures, or proving a
compatible approximation that retains them, remains a separate obligation.
No argument in this note uses a conjectured regular stratification,
replaces the surface conditional laws by uniform measures, or invokes an
unproved limiting passage from polytopes.

## 8. Tight support only on a measurable contact subset

The regular chart need not be contained in the contact set. Keep the
C^2 normal chart, C^2 support heights, and actual surface Jacobian
hypotheses, but let

    Z={t in U:h_0(t)=[h_-(t)+h_+(t)]/2}.

Suppose the same-normal crossflow is concentrated on Z. Its normal
marginal on this patch is absolutely continuous with respect to dt by
(8), so it suffices to work at Lebesgue density points of Z.

Let g=h_0-(h_-+h_+)/2. Convex midpoint inclusion gives g>=0, and g=0
on Z. At every point of Z, grad g=0 because that point is a minimum.
At a density point t of Z one also has D^2g(t)=0. Indeed if this
positive semidefinite Hessian were nonzero, its quadratic form would
be strictly positive on a fixed cone of directions. Taylor's formula
would then give g(t+h)>0 for all sufficiently small nonzero h in a
slightly smaller cone, excluding a fixed positive fraction of every
small ball from Z, contrary to density one.

Thus at almost every t of Z the values, gradients, and Hessians of h_0
are the averages of those of h_- and h_+. The canonical face origins
therefore average, and the matrices Q_i obey (9). All conditional
capacity and repair conclusions follow at those t. This removes an
open-contact assumption; it does not remove the regular-foliation and
actual-Jacobian hypotheses.
